summary: PR 1110 at 090cc57059021edb34acd063d7ba2ab7f3ab8a2d replaces inherited zero accounting with physical-tensor accounting for DeepSeek-V4 pools and fixes the remaining HiSparse uint64 device-pointer-table omission. Real gfx950 allocations and independent pipeline-slice cases matched exactly.

tests.what_was_measured: Reproduced the original failure with real GPU tensors: non-unified FP8 owned 3,594,944 bytes while base mem_usage reported 0.
Six tests and ten subtests passed, including one- and three-layer HiSparse pointer-table accounting plus top-level unified/non-unified aggregation boundaries.
Actual gfx950 FP8, ROCm FP4-indexer, HiSparse, and unified allocations all matched independent physical byte sums; HiSparse was 3,594,952 bytes with zero delta.
C4-only HiSparse, C128-only, SWA-only, mixed, and unified mixed PP slices had zero byte delta; independent enumeration also asserted unique backing-storage identities.
Candidate patch has no whitespace errors.

gpu_execution.evidence: Actual allocations ran on one AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 GPU. Raw base, candidate, and adversarial outputs are in reports/j-9d7120f197ed/evidence/.

remaining_limitations: No DeepSeek-V4 weights or 8x H100 system were available, so full HTTP serving/metric scrape, CUDA/H100, multi-rank, model-semantic, NPU, and CUDA-only online-C128 behavior remain unverified. No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
